4th Period.workingNow: Making your own copy of the ROLLER base repo, playing it, and listing what it already does.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One design document in your portfolio repo bringing together your mechanics, dynamics, aesthetic and state map — plus your ROLLER game embedded and playable on your portfolio site — pushed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can name the mechanics of a game so that I can describe what my mod will add to the base game.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Decompose problems and subproblems into parts to facilitate the design, implementation, and review of programs.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Overview + copy the ROLLER base repo (10 min)
You do: play it, list what it already does (10 min)
I do / We do: the M in MDA (15 min)
You do: 3 mechanics your mod adds (8 min)
Exit Ticket: your best mechanic (2 min)
4th Period.connections: Your AI article is published — that detour is done. Today you get the base game every mod this semester is built on: a circle that rolls, jumps, and dies on spikes. Before you change it you have to be able to say exactly what it already does. Tomorrow you finish the design, and the rest of the semester you build it.

6th Period.workingNow: Picking one thing and naming exactly two states it can be in.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your completed Game Plan document — two mechanics each with a number, five states, how the mechanics connect to the states, and your first level described — typed and turned in by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can name two states of one thing so that I can describe it without describing everything at once.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Overview: a new way to describe things (3 min)
I do: what a state is — the lamp (12 min)
We do: name the states of 3 everyday things (12 min)
You do: pick your thing, name 2 states (15 min)
6th Period.connections: Your game design plan is turned in. This week we slow all the way down and learn the one idea that makes a game actually run: a state. Today you only need two of them. By Friday you will have five, and next week you use them to build with SchoolAI.
